Fatty Liver Disease

aspartate aminotransferase (AST):alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ratio · causes to exclude · fibrosis staging · weight loss first · formerly nonalcoholic fatty liver diseaseIs the picture metabolic with ALT above AST, and have the other liver diseases been excluded?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Illness script
Bottom line
  • Metabolic risk factors with ALT above AST (ratio usually under 1) and a bright liver on ultrasound is MASLD once alcohol, viral hepatitis, iron overload and drugs are excluded.
  • Stage fibrosis noninvasively: the Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4), then elastography; biopsy when the diagnosis or stage is unclear or portal hypertension is unexplained.
  • Weight loss of 7 to 10% treats the liver; statins are safe and are used for dyslipidemia, since cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death.
What it is

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) or fatty liver: a fatty liver with at least one cardiometabolic risk factor and little or no alcohol.

Driver

Insulin resistance: free fatty acids flood the liver and hepatocytes make new fat.

Triggers

Obesity, the strongest; type 2 diabetes mellitus; dyslipidemia and hypertension

; older age

non-modifiable

; male sex, Hispanic or Native American ancestry

non-modifiable

Chain

Fat accumulates in hepatocytes (steatosis)

ballooned hepatocytes and inflammation: metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), formerly nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH)

stellate cells lay down fibrosis

cirrhosis with portal hypertension

hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)

Insights

Fibrosis stage, not fat or enzyme level, predicts liver death; AST rising above ALT suggests advanced fibrosis.

Cardiovascular disease, not liver failure, is the most common cause of death, so statins are used for dyslipidemia, not avoided.

2Urgent risks
Act now
FindingAction
Splenomegaly or low platelets in a patient with fatty liverAdvanced fibrosis may be present: splenomegaly is usually the first sign of portal hypertension. Stage now: FIB-4, then elastography; biopsy if the cause is unclear.
Normal examination in long-standing MASLDDoes not exclude cirrhosis: MASH cirrhosis can be silent, so stage every patient (step 4).
3Differential
Other causes of a fatty liver
DiagnosisDecides itNext best step
Alcohol-associated liver diseaseAST:ALT 2 or more; more than 2 drinks a day (women) or 3 (men)Obtain a corroborated drinking history; abstinence can reverse the steatosis.
Drug-induced steatosisAmiodarone, methotrexate, tamoxifen, glucocorticoids or valproate on the listReview the drug list and stop the drug where possible.
Chronic hepatitis B or CPositive hepatitis B surface antigen or hepatitis C virus antibodyViral hepatitis workup; the serology is part of the first panel (step 4).
Hereditary hemochromatosisHigh ferritin; ferritin alone also rises in MASHCheck transferrin saturation; if high, order genetic testing.
Wilson diseaseLow ceruloplasmin, Kayser-Fleischer ringsMeasure urinary copper; covers the workup.
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext best step
AST at least twice the ALTAlcohol-associated liver diseaseObtain a corroborated drinking history; abstinence can reverse the steatosis.
Mildly raised ferritinCommon in MASHCheck transferrin saturation for hemochromatosis.
Low ceruloplasmin with Kayser-Fleischer ringsWilson diseaseMeasure urinary copper.
High low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol in MASLDCardiovascular risk, the leading cause of deathStart a statin (step 7).

Pause point. The bait: normal liver enzymes seem to exclude MASLD, but enzyme levels are often normal in it.

5Diagnostic criteria
MASLD requires
CriterionRequires
SteatosisOn imaging, blood markers or biopsy
Cardiometabolic factorAt least 1 of the 5 below
Limited alcoholNo more than 2 drinks a day (women) or 3 (men)
No other causeViral hepatitis, iron overload, Wilson disease, autoimmune hepatitis, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, drugs
Cardiometabolic factors
FactorCutoff
WeightBody mass index (BMI) over 25, over 23 in Asian patients, or a large waist
GlucoseFasting over 100 mg/dL, hemoglobin A1c over 5.7%, or diabetes
Blood pressureOver 130/85 mm Hg or treated
TriglyceridesOver 150 mg/dL or treated
High-density lipoprotein (HDL)Under 40 mg/dL (men) or 50 (women)

Board stems still call it a diagnosis of exclusion. In practice: the newer criteria are positive ones, steatosis plus a cardiometabolic factor; in them hepatitis serology is helpful but not required, while the first workup still takes an alcohol and drug history and tests for hepatitis B and C.

6Severity
Stage and meaning
FindingMeaning
Simple steatosisUsually silent; progresses to MASH in 12 to 40%
MASHRisk of fibrosis, cirrhosis and HCC; it can regress to steatosis
Moderate to severe fibrosis (stage F2 to F3)Resmetirom candidate (step 7)
AST rising above ALTSuggests advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, or another cause
CirrhosisHighest liver risk: HCC and varices (step 8 gives the follow-up)
7Treatment
1

EveryoneEvery patient with MASLD

Diet and exercise for 7 to 10% weight loss; avoid alcohol; treat diabetes and dyslipidemia. A 3 to 5% loss improves the fat; 7 to 10% is needed to reduce the inflammation and fibrosis.

2

DyslipidemiaDyslipidemia

Statin: no added risk of serious liver injury in MASLD.

3

ObesityBMI 35 or more, or 30 or more with type 2 diabetes

Bariatric surgery. In one study, MASH resolved in 85% within a year of surgery.

4

FibrosisMASH with stage F2 to F3 fibrosis

Add resmetirom, a thyroid hormone beta receptor agonist. In practice: preliminary evidence suggests pioglitazone and vitamin E can improve histology in MASH but may not reduce fibrosis, and high-dose vitamin E is avoided in diabetes; glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) drugs are under study; metformin and ursodeoxycholic acid are not proven for the liver.

8Follow-up
After diagnosis
SituationDo
Lifestyle change startedRepeat liver enzymes and ultrasound in 6 to 12 months
Low fibrosis risk, abnormalities persistCBC, liver enzymes, lipids, glucose and a fibrosis score every 12 to 24 months
Advanced fibrosis or cirrhosisConsider hepatology referral; in cirrhosis, ultrasound for HCC; screen for varices
Practice
  1. 48 yo M, BMI 34, type 2 diabetes, ALT 70, AST 45, hyperechoic liver → MASLD
  2. 48 yo M with AST 180 and ALT 70 and a history of heavy drinking → Alcohol-associated liver disease → AST:ALT of 2 or more
  3. 48 yo M with MASLD asking what most improves liver histology → 7 to 10% weight loss
  4. 48 yo M with MASLD and a high FIB-4 score → Assess fibrosis with elastography
  5. 48 yo M with MASLD and low-density lipoprotein 160 → Statins are safe and indicated
  6. 32 yo M with fatty liver, low ceruloplasmin and Kayser-Fleischer rings → Wilson disease
Pearls Significant alcohol: more than 2 drinks a day (women) or 3 (men) · gallstones in pregnancy are common (progesterone → gallbladder stasis) and usually incidental without wall thickening, fever, or pain · young patient with steatosis + tremor + Kayser-Fleischer rings → Wilson disease.
Pairs with Wilson Disease covers the copper exclusion: is the patient under about 40, with a tremor, psychiatric change or Kayser-Fleischer rings, and is the ceruloplasmin low?
